title: News Kit Addons For Elementor < 1.4.9 — Subscriber+ missing authorization (plugin install/activate + arbitrary post-meta write)

exposure.note: WordPress front controller. Both actions are reachable at /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php by any authenticated Subscriber+; the required nonce leaks on every wp-admin page via the plugin's admin script loader.

affected_technologies.note: Both flaws confirmed against 1.4.7. WPScan lists CVE-2026-97352 as fixed in 1.4.9 and CVE-2026-97353 as <= 1.4.7 'no known fix', but the 1.4.9 release adds a capability check to update_mega_menu_form() as well, so 1.4.9 fixes both.
Host CMS running the vulnerable plugin.

preconditions: News Kit Addons For Elementor < 1.4.9 active (Elementor active is the realistic deployment; the plugin localizes its admin nonce once Elementor is loaded).
The attacker holds an account with at least the Subscriber role (able to load a wp-admin page such as profile.php to read the leaked nonce).
CVE-2026-97352 additionally requires outbound access to downloads.wordpress.org and that blaze-demo-importer is not already installed.

log_monitoring_urls.reason: CVE-2026-97353 — writes attacker-chosen post meta (menu=<post id>, formData=[{name,value}]).

request_body_signatures: action=nekit_install_importer with option=install|activate on an admin-ajax.php POST.
action=nekit_update_mega_menu_form with a menu=<numeric post id> and a formData JSON array of {"name":...,"value":...} entries.
Either action invoked from an authenticated session whose user lacks install_plugins / edit_theme_options (Subscriber/Contributor/Author).
behavioral: blaze-demo-importer appearing in the installed/active plugin list without an administrator action.
Unexpected post meta written to posts (arbitrary keys, or protected core keys such as _wp_page_template) not matching any editorial change.
nekit_* admin AJAX calls originating from Subscriber/Contributor/Author sessions.
A Subscriber session loading wp-admin pages (profile.php) and then issuing nekit_* AJAX writes.

remediation.primary: Upgrade News Kit Addons For Elementor to >= 1.4.9.
steps: Update the plugin to 1.4.9 or later (WP Admin > Plugins, or wp plugin update news-kit-elementor-addons). 1.4.9 adds capability checks to the admin AJAX handlers (install_plugins/activate_plugins on install_importer, edit_theme_options on update_mega_menu_form) and stops printing the nekit-admin-nonce to lower-privilege roles.
Audit the plugin list for blaze-demo-importer and remove it if it was not installed deliberately.
Review posts for unexpected or protected post meta (e.g. _wp_page_template) written by non-editorial accounts.

Review access logs for admin-ajax.php POSTs carrying action=nekit_install_importer or action=nekit_update_mega_menu_form from non-administrator sessions, and audit low-privilege (Subscriber/Contributor) accounts.
mitigations_if_upgrade_impossible: Deploy the WAF virtual patch below to block the nekit_install_importer and nekit_update_mega_menu_form actions for non-administrator sessions.
Restrict or review self-registration so untrusted users cannot obtain Subscriber accounts.
Block direct access to /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php for the nekit_* state-changing actions at the edge where only administrators are expected to use them.

signatures.description: CVE-2026-97352 — plugin install/activate action lacking a capability check in < 1.4.9.
CVE-2026-97353 — arbitrary post-meta write action lacking a capability check in <= 1.4.7.

waf.combine: block any POST to /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php where action is nekit_install_importer or nekit_update_mega_menu_form unless the session belongs to an administrator.
waf.false_positive_notes: Legitimate use of these actions comes only from administrators on the plugin's own screens. After upgrading to 1.4.9 the plugin enforces capability checks server-side, so blocking non-admin callers is safe.
